headline: Time-explicit models relate developmental pace, protein epistasis and B cell lineages
label: Time Resolved Evolutionary Modeling
summary: Three new studies apply explicit time-resolved models to developmental aging, protein evolution and B cell lineage tracing.
synthesis: The common thread across these three items is explicit modeling of time in evolutionary and developmental processes rather than assuming uniform rates. A preprint aligns 11,365 human and canid observations across organ systems and finds that system-level heterochrony models outperform the rule of seven for translating developmental and aging timing between species. A published continuous-time protein evolution model uses Gillespie simulation parameterized by a Potts generative model to reveal epistatic signatures in sequence evolution. TyCHE, a Bayesian phylogenetics package, infers time-resolved lineage trees in which clock rates are linked to discrete states, and is applied to B cell populations alongside its SimBLE simulator. What is new in each case is the coupling of rate or timing parameters to an explicit structure: organ-system heterochrony, epistatic constraint, or discrete cellular state. The items report methods and inference frameworks, not deployed outcomes.
